morning.text:
A design prize is not a client contract. Know the difference before you enter.

How it works and where to start:
https://insightginie.com/earn/design-competitions/

Submit original work to a contest after reviewing its prize and rights conditions.

Who pays: Clients running a design contest

Try one small step: Compare the time commitment, selection process and rights before entering one suitable contest.

The catch: Most entrants do not win. Contest work is speculative, and platform eligibility, entry rules and intellectual-property terms apply.

A method to explore, not an available paid assignment. Selection, demand and earnings vary.

evening.text:
A $10 spreadsheet needs more than 20 sales to repay $200 of your time.

The guide and practical first step:
https://insightginie.com/earn/sell-spreadsheets/

Illustrative maths: assume 10 hours of work valued at $20 per hour, a $10 selling price and hypothetical fees of 10%. Each sale leaves $9 before tax and other costs. Twenty-two sales leave $198; twenty-three leave $207.

Try this: Calculate your own break-even sales before spending a weekend building a digital product.

These are assumptions, not a platform fee quote or an earnings forecast. Refunds, support and other costs would increase the target.

Illustrative calculation: InsightGinie original worked example; Gumroad is one possible selling platform. Original reference and review date are in the guide.
